text:
Pause on M-eight-module for a complete
evidence reading of Experiment

M — Eight-module LLM landscape. First,
identify the research question

before looking at the answer. The question
asks whether the

fixed components create a meaningful
ordering surface, whether a particular

neighborhood provides useful guidance on
that surface, or whether a

cheaper executor is equally effective. The
sample is 20 questions,
and the source artifact is

experiments/iteration-11/results/search_results.csv.
The horizontal axis

names the recorded independent
quantity—such as permutation size,

distance, or distinct evaluations. The
vertical axis names the measured

outcome—such as accuracy, error, hit
probability, regret, correlation, or

hitting time. Raw points remain visible
when their count permits.

A summary line or bar describes those
points; it does

not replace them. A capped observation
receives a censor marker,

and a sampled landscape never pretends to
be exhaustively enumerated.

The central pattern supports this finding:
Gate result: accuracy 0.10–1.00,

standard deviation 0.240. The correct
limitation is: Lesson: only 20

questions made the accuracy grid coarse
and exact optima dense.

That limitation rules out a broader
promotional interpretation while

preserving the result actually measured.
The decision carried into the

research program is: Carry this constraint
into the next experiment

and compare methods at equal cost.
Finally, compare against the

equal-budget alternative. Generations,
repeated cache hits, and distinct

evaluations are not interchangeable. A
method earns a search-efficiency

claim only when uncertainty, evaluator
resolution, optimum density, and

evaluation cost have all been accounted
for.
